title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by PowerShell on scranton and wsmprovhost on nashua
rationale: All these findings anchor on the same LSASS handle-access events: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) opening lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:05:16, and wsmprovhost.exe opening lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:09:29, with matching Security 4656/4663 events showing read-from-process-memory access masks. This is the classic LSASS memory credential-dump pattern, best fitting T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).

title: lsass.exe writes C:\Windows\debug\PASSWD.LOG on scranton
rationale: On scranton.dmevals.local, lsass.exe (SYSTEM) created C:\Windows\debug\PASSWD.LOG during the intrusion window, consistent with credential material being written out from LSASS memory, fitting T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).

title: Sysinternals pspasswd/accesschk credential collection creating 'passwordsDB' on scranton
rationale: PowerShell (user pbeesly) wrote Sysinternals pspasswd64.exe/pspasswd.exe and ran accesschk.exe, which created the file C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB on scranton.dmevals.local. pspasswd is a password tool and the passwordsDB artifact indicates local account credential material collection, best fitting T1003.002 (Security Account Manager).

title: Forced authentication via SMB/WebDAV coercion from scranton to attacker-controlled 192.168.0.4
rationale: Host 10.0.1.4 (scranton.dmevals.local) attempted SMB to 192.168.0.4:445 (rejected) then fell back to WebDAV over HTTP using the Windows WebDAV redirector, issuing OPTIONS/PROPFIND/PUT/LOCK/PROPPATCH/HEAD/UNLOCK with an AUTHORIZATION header. This coerced authentication to an attacker-controlled host is T1187 (Forced Authentication).

title: Explicit-credential logons (4648) using pbeesly credentials via PsExec
rationale: Event 4648 explicit-credential logons for pbeesly originating from 10.0.1.6 on scranton and via PSEXESVC.exe on nashua are consistent with reuse of harvested credentials; the credential material itself is used from tooling/scripts, best fitting T1552.001 (Credentials In Files) among in-scope techniques.

title: Hardcoded credentials in Invoke-Exfil used to mount attacker WebDAV share
rationale: The Invoke-Exfil PowerShell script block on scranton.dmevals.local contains embedded plaintext credentials ($UserName='cozy', $Password='MyCozyPassw0rd!') used to map \\192.168.0.4\webdav. Credentials embedded in files/scripts fit T1552.001 (Credentials In Files).

title: Rar.exe password-protected archive of credential-bearing loot on nashua
rationale: On nashua.dmevals.local, Rar.exe (user pbeesly) created a password-protected archive of collected data, later wiped with sdelete64. This is staging of harvested credential/browser-store data, best fitting T1555.003 (Credentials from Web Browsers).

title: Anomalous krbtgt service-ticket requests from SCRANTON$ on newyork
rationale: On newyork.dmevals.local, machine account SCRANTON$ requested Kerberos service tickets for the krbtgt service with TicketOptions 0x60810010, an unusual pattern consistent with forged/abused ticket activity (golden-ticket style), fitting T1558.001.

title: PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificates to .pfx files on scranton
rationale: User pbeesly ran a PowerShell script block defining Get-PrivateKeys that enumerates cert:\LocalMachine and exports every certificate with Export-PfxCertificate to randomly named .pfx files protected by hardcoded password 'saribas', with a resulting .pfx file observed. Stealing authentication certificates fits T1649.

title: Related malicious activity in window is not network sniffing (PsExec lateral movement, python C2, screen capture)
rationale: The window contains PsExec64.exe with plaintext credentials to \\NASHUA spawning python.exe via PSEXESVC that beaconed to 192.168.0.4:8443, plus screen capture and steganography decoding and sdelete64 wiping. This is lateral movement/remote services rather than credential access, so out-of-scope:T1021.002 (SMB/Windows Admin Shares).

title: Intrusion chain on scranton: malicious .scr, hidden PowerShell, Invoke-Exfil, sdelete cleanup
rationale: A malicious screen-saver .scr launched from explorer.exe spawned cmd.exe and hidden PowerShell that decoded a payload from monkey.png, compiled code with csc.exe, ran Invoke-Discovery/Invoke-Exfil, and deleted the .scr with sdelete64. This is user execution of a malicious file, not credential access, so out-of-scope:T1204 (User Execution).
